title: Instruction contract
description: One instruction contract. Contracts are authored as decorator kwargs and live as in-memory dicts, so this describes the serializable subset of such a dict — a callable field such as on_cancel is not JSON-representable and is checked Python-side instead.

opcode.description: Namespaced identifier, exactly two segments. Uniqueness across the instruction set is the registry's job, not this schema's.

description.description: What the instruction does, in prose. Read by a composer choosing between instructions.

inputs.description: The inputs this instruction accepts. An empty map states outright that it takes nothing.

outputs.description: The outputs this instruction produces. An empty map states outright that it returns nothing.

side_effect.description: Whether running this instruction changes state outside the program. Coarse by design: policy gates on opcode, not on effect class.

visibility.description: The trust boundary. composable instructions may be reached by an untrusted composer; internal ones may be called only by trusted first-party code.

examples.description: At least one worked example. Registration without one is a failure, so it is required here rather than only at registration.

inputs.description: Input values keyed by parameter name, as a caller would supply them.

outputs.description: The output values the instruction produces for those inputs, keyed by output name.

anyOf.description: An example states its expectation by giving concrete outputs. Further ways of stating one are added as further alternatives here, leaving this one untouched.

critical_default.description: Fallback for a node's critical flag when the node omits it.

deps.description: Names of container-registered dependencies this instruction is handed at call time. Names registered in the boot container — not opcodes, and not Python package names.
